result: The authors surveyed 39 ab1 sensilla (>80% of the population) in a single antenna using SBEM, finding substantial heterogeneity in dendritic branch counts (65-295 branches, CV=0.22) but less variability in cuticle morphometrics (CV=0.06-0.10). No correlation was found between dendritic number and sensillum cross-sectional area, suggesting independent regulation of these features.
evaluation: All reviewers acknowledge the comprehensive population-level survey and accept the finding of dendritic heterogeneity. Reviewer 1 states the study 'convincingly finding significant structural variation both within and across distinct classes,' and Reviewer 2 notes 'the authors use this analysis to...provide evidence of substantial morphological diversity even within a single subclass of neuron.' The quantitative measurements and statistical analyses are not questioned.

result: ab1C CO2-sensing neurons exhibit unique flattened, sheet-like dendritic morphology distinct from cylindrical odor-sensing neurons, with remarkable morphological diversity categorized into four types (loosely curled, fully curled, split, and mixed). The flattened segment has a surface area-to-volume ratio over 300% higher than the cylindrical segment (23.94 vs 7.58).
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly support this finding. Reviewer 2 states 'The study makes a convincing case that ab1C neurons exhibit a unique, dendritic morphology unlike the canonical cylindrical dendrites found in ab1D neurons.' Reviewer 3 notes 'the authors discovered that there is a difference between CO2- and odour sensing neurons of which the first show a characteristic flattened and sheet-like structure not observed in other sensory neurons.' The morphometric quantification and classification scheme are accepted without challenge.

result: ab1D odor-sensing neurons show significant heterogeneity in dendritic branching, with 38% having unbranched dendrites and 62% having 2-7 branches. Branching points varied widely (8-44% of cuticle length, CV=0.46), while termination was less variable (63-97%, CV=0.09).
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding as part of the overall demonstration of morphological heterogeneity. Reviewer 3 states 'Their data convincingly shows that there is dendritic heterogenity in both investigated populations and their sample size is sufficient to strongly support this observation.' The quantitative measurements are not questioned by any reviewer.

result: The authors speculate that the increased surface area-to-volume ratio in ab1C flattened dendrites could enhance CO2 detection capacity and signal propagation, and that morphological diversity may expand functional adaptability of homotypic ORNs. However, morphometric features did not differ significantly among ab1C morphological categories.
evaluation: All reviewers note the lack of functional validation. Reviewer 2 states 'The biggest question remains unanswered: whether structural variation observed in the ab1C dendrites by SBEM have an electrophysiological functional relevance?' Reviewer 1 acknowledges 'this was not directly tested in their study due to technical limitations.' Reviewer 3 notes 'current methods prevent linking morphology to odour sensitivity or other properties of the neurons.' The speculation is acknowledged but unvalidated.

result: Morphometric analysis of ab1D neurons revealed that branching increases total sensory surface area by 49% while providing only modest enhancement in surface area-to-volume ratio (14%). Within branched neurons, distal segments showed 250% higher SA/V ratio than proximal segments. Individual branch dimensions remained consistent regardless of branch number, suggesting structural scaling preserves biophysical properties.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the detailed morphometric quantification without challenge. Reviewer 1 notes 'This work provides a thorough morphometric analysis' and Reviewer 3 states 'The volumetric EM imaging and reconstruction approach offers unprecedented details in single cell morphology.' The functional interpretations about biophysical properties are presented as speculation and reviewers acknowledge the descriptive nature of the study.

result: The three auxiliary cells (thecogen, trichogen, tormogen) in ab1 sensilla follow a conserved organization similar to other sensilla types, with some differences: the thecogen separates individual ORN inner dendrites (unlike ab4), and the tormogen lacks a stalk-like protrusion (unlike ab4 and ac3).
evaluation: These structural observations are not questioned by any reviewer. The findings are presented as descriptive anatomical details that complement the main neuronal morphology results. No reviewer raises concerns about these auxiliary cell characterizations.

result: The authors conclude that morphological heterogeneity is common among homotypic ORNs, and that while these neurons exhibit characteristic dendritic motifs, their morphologies are more variable than previously assumed.
evaluation: All reviewers accept this as a major conclusion. Reviewer 1 states the study 'reveals surprising morphological diversity of Drosophila sensory neurons.' Reviewer 3 notes 'This data proposes that the phenomenon of dendritic heterogenity is common in the Drosophila olfactory system and will stimulate future investigations.' The conclusion is well-supported by the population-level data.

result: The authors generated a new SBEM volume encompassing nearly the entire antenna using the CryoChem method with high-pressure freezing, which provides superior morphological preservation compared to chemical fixation for tissues with cuticles.
evaluation: While reviewers acknowledge the technical quality, Reviewer 2 raises concerns about potential artifacts: 'Although Cryofixation is superior to chemical fixation...all types of fixations in TEMs cause some artifacts, as does serial sectioning. An understanding of the error rates for the SBEM method would have increased the confidence in the conclusions drawn.' The method is accepted but with noted limitations.
